title: AmberWave Manufacturing private deploy - cutover checklist and TF adapters (WIP)
content:
Status: working draft (internal playbook). Owner: Priya Shenoy. Purpose: capture AmberWave Manufacturing private deployment assumptions, sizing, Terraform adapter notes, and a pragmatic cutover/rollback plan for their VPC + on-prem hybrid deployment.

Background/context:
- AmberWave is deploying Redwood Private in their primary production VPC (eu-west-1) with a DR colo (on-prem) in the same country for regulatory reasons.
- Requirements: low-latency local inference for factory-floor telemetry (99th percentile < 80ms for short prompts), data never leaves customer network, hardware mix: 2x A10G equivalent on prem + 4x A10G in cloud dedicated hosts (initial).
- SLA expectation: 99.9% uptime, burstable throughput to 200 concurrent inference sessions, predictable unit economics.

Goals for this doc:
1) Rough sizing and performance targets for pilot and production phases.
2) Terraform module integration notes (what adapters to add and variables to override).
3) Cutover checklist for pilot -> canary -> full production.
4) Risk register, rollback triggers, and test plan.

Key assumptions (call these out to AmberWave before sign-off):
- Payload profile: median input length 120 tokens, median response 40 tokens, 80% of requests are synchronous low-latency calls.
- Model baseline: open-llama-13b-8k quantized variant (customer requested to start with an open model). Performance numbers assume int8 quantized variant.
- Network: site has dedicated fiber link, BGP with cloud provider for failover. Inter-region latency between on-prem colo and eu-west-1 is ~12ms RTT.
- Storage: model artifacts will be stored in S3-compatible object store in VPC; on-prem will have cached local copies on NVMe.
- KMS: AmberWave will provide AWS KMS for cloud and an HSM appliance (Luna/Thales style) on-prem; we will integrate via Redwood KMS/HSM adapters.

Sizing recommendation (pilot -> prod):
- Pilot (2-week): 1 shard on-prem (2x A10G), 1 cloud shard (2x A10G), test datasets only, sample traffic up to 20 rps.
- Canary (6-week): 2 on-prem shards (4x A10G total), 2 cloud shards (4x A10G), synthetic load up to 80 rps, run mixed live traffic at 10% of production.
- Prod initial (GA): 3 on-prem shards (6x A10G), 4 cloud shards (8x A10G), autoscaling policies configured for reserved baseline + burst to 200 concurrent sessions.
- Headroom: plan for 30% headroom on token throughput and 40% on memory for KV cache growth.
- Disk: each on-prem node needs 1.5TB NVMe for model cache, plus 2TB for logs/metrics retention (local short-term).

Performance targets and acceptance criteria:
- P99 latency for 1–512 token requests: <= 80ms on-prem under sustained baseline load (measured with our probe harness).
- Token throughput: baseline 50k tokens/min per A10G shard.
- Startup time for model on cold start: < 25s (we will pre-warm during cutover).
- Regression gates: if model quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM eval set) drops > 5% vs baseline, block rollout.

Terraform adapter notes (what we changed / need to upstream):
- Module: redwood-private/shards -> forked as amberwave/redwood-private-shards-adapter. Key vars overridden:
  - instance_type (A10G -> amberwave-specific SKU mapping),
  - mgmt_subnet_ids (customer-provided),
  - kms_key_arn (accepts HSM alias or cloud KMS ARN),
  - local_cache_path (NVMe mount path var),
  - prewarm_image (AMI/container image id for pre-warm step).
- New small helper module: network-peering-with-onprem - creates route table entries and BGP session stubs (customer will fill BGP creds).
- Secrets handling: switched from remote_state outputs to direct SSM Parameter Store encrypted by KMS for a short window during bootstrapping. Docs: see PR 78 for code snippets.
- Recommended TF workflow: use workspace per environment (pilot/canary/prod) and short-lived plan players for cutover. Locking via remote state + DynamoDB.
- Items to upstream later: a generic kms-provider interface in redwood modules to accept HSM provider endpoints (currently cloud-only).

Networking summary (diagram referenced in Confluence):
- On-prem: private VLAN for Redwood nodes. Management NIC on DMZ with restricted API access.
- Cloud: dedicated VPC with private subnets for shards and transit gateway attached.
- Connectivity: primary BGP session between on-prem edge and TGW; fallback over IPsec VPN to different AZ.
- Firewall: only allow ports 22 (jumpbox), 443 (control plane), 4510-4520 (inference control plane RPC) between cloud <-> onprem.

Storage and caching notes:
- Model artifacts: store canonical artifacts in S3-compatible store in cloud. Use a cached local NVMe-based model cache on each shard.
- Upload/download strategy: use rsync from S3 gateway to on-prem cache during maintenance windows.
- Persistence for small-size KV cache snapshots: persist to on-prem NFS endpoint daily for faster warm restarts.

KMS / HSM integration:
- Cloud path: standard AWS KMS CMKs used for S3 envelope encryption and secrets.
- On-prem: support for PKCS#11 HSM. We will use the redwood-kms-adapter which expects endpoint + client cert. AmberWave must provide network access and credential rotation plan.
- Key ceremony: recommend a joint call during canary to validate key import and rotation scripts.

Upgrade and rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 - Preflight (2 weeks):
- Run preflight script (network checks, disk IO, GPU driver/firmware versions).
- Confirm BGP sessions and routing tables.
- Validate KMS/HSM handshake.
- TF plan applied in pilot workspace, observe no drift.

Phase 1 - Pilot (2 weeks):
- Deploy 1 on-prem shard + 1 cloud shard.
- Run perf tests, end-to-end QA, synthetic replay of 10k historical requests.
- Collect telemetry, SLOs, and cost metrics.

Phase 2 - Canary (6 weeks):
- Scale to canary sizing.
- Route 10% live traffic through canary shards with feature flags.
- Monitor quality/regressions and latency.
- Run a full backup of KV caches before canary testing.

Phase 3 - Incremental Cutover (2 weeks):
- Gradual traffic ramp from 10% -> 50% -> 100% across rolling windows.
- Keep autoscaler conservative: prefer adding shards not reducing.
- Execute acceptance tests after each ramp.

Phase 4 - Post-cutover hardening (4 weeks):
- Run extended soak, tune batching/caching, and measure cost per token.

Rollback strategy and automated triggers:
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - P99 latency > 150ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows,
  - Error rate increase > 3x baseline for 10 minutes,
  - Model quality regression gate fails.
- Rollback actions: immediate traffic switch to previous model variant and/or region fallback to cloud-only model pool.
- Manual rollback: redeploy previous TF workspace snapshot and restore KV cache snapshot (timestamped).

Cutover checklist (operational runbook):
- Pre-cutover:
  - Confirm PR 78 merged and TF workspace pilot applied.
  - All participants on zoom + shared Slack channel.
  - Backup snapshots of KV caches and model artifacts taken and verified.
  - HSM/KMS health check complete.
  - Monitoring probes (loadgen) configured and running.
- During cutover:
  - Sequentially bring shards into service, validate health endpoints after each boot.
  - Run smoke test suite (sanity + eval prompts).
  - Confirm telemetry flow to Datadog + long-term archive.
- Post-cutover:
  - Run full eval harness across customer prompt set.
  - Confirm cost dashboard metrics in Redwood Console.
  - Hand off to AmberWave SRE with runbooks and escalation contacts.

Observability and SLOs:
- Instrumentation: per-request tracing, per-shard token counters, cold-start metrics, KV cache hit ratio.
- Dashboards: latency distribution, per-route error breakdown, token cost per model.
- Alerting: P99 latency, error rate, disk pressure, GPU driver faults.

Testing matrix (minimum):
- Perf: synthetic rps ramping to expected peak + 30% headroom.
- Chaos: simulate loss of one on-prem shard and validate failover to cloud in <60s.
- Security: pen test of control plane access, KMS cert expiry simulation.
- Data residency: verify no telemetry contains customer PII outside their network.

Open questions / decisions needed from AmberWave:
1) Final approval for instance SKUs and whether they will accept our A10G-equivalent suggestion or provide specific hardware procurement.
2) Confirmation on how long HSM credentials can be shared during initial bootstrap (recommend ephemeral creds with rotation).
3) Retention policy for local logs and whether we need cross-site log aggregation.
4) Will AmberWave provide a caching NFS, or should we deploy a small EBS-backed cache cluster?

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: on-prem NIC firmware mismatch causes GPU drivers to misbehave. Mitigation: preflight firmware check, deploy with conservative driver versions.
- Risk: HSM handshake failure. Mitigation: schedule key ceremony and fallback to KMS-wrapped local keys for limited window.
- Risk: under-provisioned KV cache causing cold-start spikes. Mitigation: prewarm strategy and persistent cache snapshots.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- AmberWave: confirm hardware SKU list and BGP creds (owner: AmberWave NetOps) - ETA: 2025-02-20.
- Redwood eng: open PR to add kms-provider interface to redwood modules (owner: Marco) - ETA: 2025-02-28.
- Site reliability: write the cutover runbook and test checklist (owner: Sofia) - ETA: 2025-03-05.

Appendix A - Terraform snippets (high level):
- Use workspace = "pilot" / "canary" / "prod"
- Example variable override:
  module "shard" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-terraform-modules.git//shard?ref=amberwave-adapter"
    instance_type = var.amber_instance_type
    mgmt_subnet_ids = var.amber_mgmt_subnets
    kms_key_arn = var.amber_kms_arn
    local_cache_path = "/mnt/nvme/models"
  }

Appendix B - Quick checklist for TF operators:
- run terraform plan -> save plan artifact with timestamp.
- apply in pilot workspace first.
- do not destroy pilot workspace until prod soak complete.

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Add wiring diagram exported from Sketch to Confluence (visual).
- Schedule KMS key ceremony and get HSM logs access.
- Confirm whether AmberWave wants automatic quantization suggestions enabled in Redwood Optimize.

References:
- PR 78: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-terraform-modules/pull/78
- AmberWave contract excerpt (internal) - CONFLUENCE-AMP-PRIVATE-DEPLOY-PLAN

End of draft.

-- Priya
